jurisdiction.name: Sweden
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Sweden steers AI mainly through its first comprehensive AI Strategy and action plan, adopted by the government in February 2026 under the Ministry of Finance and built on the AI Commission's 2025 roadmap, following the 2018 national approach to AI. Its law implementing the EU AI Act is still pending after a 2025 inquiry proposed the Post and Telecom Authority (PTS) as coordinating authority with a sandbox; the one AI-specific statute so far is a 2026 law on real-time facial recognition by law enforcement, with each use notified to the data protection authority. The Agency for Digital Government (Digg) and the data protection authority (IMY) have issued guidelines on generative AI in public administration, the Administrative Procedure Act allows automated decisions, and a new Digitalisation Authority from 2027 will guide public-sector AI use.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Sweden's law implementing the EU AI Act has not yet been presented to parliament and is listed as a lead.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Sweden (Government Offices, Ministry of Finance; responsible minister Erik Slottner)
instruments.current_status: Published 20 February 2026 (updated 26 February 2026) by the Ministry of Finance on regeringen.se, with an official English translation ('Sweden's AI Strategy', Government Offices of Sweden 2026). In force as the government's AI strategy, implemented through the separate action plan.
instruments.summary: Sweden's first comprehensive national AI strategy, built on the AI Commission's roadmap (SOU 2025:12) and the digitalisation strategy 2025-2030. It sets the goal that Sweden be among the ten leading AI nations, and organises policy under AI for societal benefit (legal framework and regulatory simplification, data access, standardisation, security and defence, a public sector in the vanguard), AI for competitiveness and innovation, and the AI ecosystem (compute, skills, research, Swedish language models). It states that the strategy is followed up annually together with the digitalisation strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; frames Sweden's approach to the EU AI Act (simple rules, no national gold-plating) and to public-sector AI use.

instruments.english_title: Action plan for Sweden's AI Strategy
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Sweden (Government Offices, Ministry of Finance)
instruments.current_status: Published 20 February 2026 on regeringen.se together with the strategy; official English translation at https://www.government.se/contentassets/4e6b2d34f81048d688c35c831065395f/action-plan-for-swedens-ai-strategy.pdf. It records that the SOU 2025:101 consultation closed on 23 February 2026.
instruments.summary: Lists adopted and planned government measures implementing the 2026 AI Strategy, most decided in 2025 and covering large parts of the AI Commission's proposals. Measures include increased funding for IMY's regulatory sandbox for AI, the inquiry on national adaptations to the EU AI Act (SOU 2025:101), data and AI assignments to over 100 agencies and higher-education institutions, a planned data-steward function at Statistics Sweden and Digg, and a planned standardisation action plan for AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Operational companion to the AI Strategy listing concrete AI governance measures and their legal/budget references.

instruments.summary: Sweden's first government AI policy document, setting an overall direction for AI work and a basis for future priorities. It sets out the government's assessments in four areas: education, research, innovation and use, and framework and infrastructure, including the need to develop rules, standards, norms and ethical principles for ethical and sustainable AI and to make data available as infrastructure for AI.

instruments.official_title: Anpassningar till AI-förordningen – Säker användning, effektiv kontroll och stöd för innovation (SOU 2025:101)
instruments.english_title: Adaptations to the AI Act – Safe use, effective control and support for innovation (SOU 2025:101)
instruments.issuing_authority: Inquiry on safe and trustworthy use of AI (Dir. 2024:83), Ministry of Finance
instruments.current_status: Published 6 October 2025 and sent for consultation on 11 November 2025 (deadline 23 February 2026). As of 12 October 2026 the government's legislative record lists no Lagrådsremiss or proposition, so no national AI Act implementing law has been adopted. Consultation closed on 23 February 2026.
instruments.summary: Government inquiry report proposing Sweden's national supplementary rules to the EU AI Act, to be gathered mainly in a new act and a new ordinance. It proposes a supervision system of eleven market surveillance authorities and two notifying authorities, with the Swedish Post and Telecom Authority (PTS) as main/coordinating market surveillance authority, rules on sanctions and interventions, and an AI regulatory sandbox to be set up by PTS, plus confidentiality provisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Draft national implementation of the EU AI Act, including designation of competent authorities.

instruments.official_title: Lag (2026:806) om användning av AI-system för ansiktsigenkänning i realtid för brottsbekämpande ändamål
instruments.english_title: Act (2026:806) on the use of AI systems for real-time facial recognition for law enforcement purposes
instruments.issuing_authority: Swedish Parliament (Riksdag), on government bill prop. 2025/26:150 (Ministry of Justice)
instruments.current_status: Issued (utfärdad) 28 May 2026 after the Riksdag adopted bet. 2025/26:JuU28 on 26 May 2026; amended by SFS 2026:807 (registration under AI Act Article 49, from a date the government decides). The committee report states a proposed entry into force of 1 July 2026; the consolidated text on riksdagen.se does not state the entry-into-force date, so no commencement date is given.
instruments.summary: Regulates the Swedish Police Authority's and Security Service's use of real-time remote biometric identification AI systems in public places, as permitted by the EU AI Act. Use is allowed only where strictly necessary for listed purposes (e.g. victims of kidnapping or trafficking, missing persons, imminent threats, suspects of serious Annex II crimes) and subject to proportionality and a permit procedure; a fundamental-rights impact assessment under AI Act Article 27 is required before first use, and identified persons must be notified.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sweden's first AI-specific statute; implements the law-enforcement biometric identification options of the EU AI Act.

instruments.english_title: Ordinance (2026:815) on the use of AI systems for real-time facial recognition for law enforcement purposes
instruments.current_status: Issued 28 May 2026; entry-into-force date not stated in the consolidated text on riksdagen.se.
instruments.summary: Supplements Act 2026:806: every use of a real-time facial recognition AI system must be notified to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) by the authority that started the use, with the information required by AI Act Article 5(4) and 5(6). It also specifies the content of notifications to identified individuals and assigns that duty to the prosecutor who applied for the permit.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Designates IMY as recipient of AI Act Article 5(4) notifications for real-time biometric identification.

instruments.english_title: Ordinance (2026:1769) with instructions for the Swedish Digitalisation Agency (Digitaliseringsmyndigheten)
instruments.current_status: Issued 3 September 2026; enters into force 1 January 2027 (transitional provision 1).
instruments.summary: Founding instruction for Digitaliseringsmyndigheten, a new agency merging the Post and Telecom Authority's and Digg's mandates, with overall responsibility for society's digitalisation and electronic communications. Under 'Data management and artificial intelligence' (§§ 16-19) it coordinates public-sector data standards and sharing and must give guidance to the rest of public administration on the use of AI (§ 19). It repeals the instructions of PTS (2007:951) and Digg (2018:1486) from 1 January 2027.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Establishes the national agency responsible for AI guidance to the public sector from 2027.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): consolidated text read in full from riksdagen.se SFS database (entry into force 1 January 2027 stated).

instruments.current_status: In force since 1 July 2018; amended up to SFS 2025:582.
instruments.summary: General administrative procedure law for Swedish public authorities. Section 28 expressly allows a decision to be made by an official alone, by several jointly, or automatically ('automatiserat'), giving the legal basis for automated decision-making by agencies, which remain subject to the Act's requirements on reasons, communication and appeal.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Explicit statutory basis for automated (including algorithmic) administrative decisions.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): consolidated text read from riksdagen.se SFS database (§ 28 and transitional provisions).

instruments.official_title: Lag (2018:218) med kompletterande bestämmelser till EU:s dataskyddsförordning
instruments.english_title: Act (2018:218) containing supplementary provisions to the EU General Data Protection Regulation
instruments.current_status: In force since 25 May 2018; amended up to SFS 2026:1589 (some amendments enter into force 1 January 2027).
instruments.summary: Sweden's Data Protection Act supplementing the GDPR: it extends GDPR rules to activities outside EU law, sets national legal bases and conditions for processing (including sensitive data and personal identity numbers), and governs supervision, administrative fines and appeals. It is the national data protection framework applying to AI training and use involving personal data, supervised by IMY.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National GDPR implementing law governing personal-data processing in AI systems.

instruments.official_title: Riktlinjer för användning av generativ AI och kompetenshöjande insatser
instruments.english_title: Guidelines for the use of generative AI and competence-raising measures
instruments.issuing_authority: Agency for Digital Government (Digg) and Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), on government assignment Fi2024/01535
instruments.current_status: Dated 20 January 2025 (Digg dnr 2024-4755) and handed to the government on 21 January 2025; described as a first version to be developed further. Digg's functions pass to Digitaliseringsmyndigheten on 1 January 2027.
instruments.summary: National guiding (non-binding) guidelines for state agencies, municipalities and regions on using generative AI, produced by Digg with IMY on a government assignment. They cover leadership and accountability, ethics, procurement, data protection, information security, copyright and labour law, and encourage use for efficiency while stressing awareness of rules, risks and responsibility, especially for sensitive data. The report also describes Digg's AI competence-raising activities for smaller public organisations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national guidance on generative AI in public administration.

instruments.official_title: GDPR vid användning av generativ AI
instruments.summary: IMY's part of the government assignment on generative-AI guidelines for public administration, explaining how public bodies can use generative AI consistently with the GDPR. It covers applying data protection principles (minimisation, transparency), allocating controller and processor roles, legal basis and necessity, automated decision-making and third-country transfers, security and DPIAs; development and fine-tuning of models are outside its scope.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection authority guidance on generative AI use by public bodies.

instruments.english_title: AI use in the Swedish financial sector
instruments.current_status: Published 6 December 2024 (Dnr 24-18158); an English version ('AI use in the Swedish financial sector') is on finansinspektionen.se.
instruments.summary: FI's survey of AI use among Swedish financial firms (234 respondents), covering staff use of generative AI, AI systems in production, concrete use cases and their risk classification under the EU AI Act. It finds rapid uptake of generative AI and concludes that firms' risk management is lagging, and sets out FI's expectations on safe and trustworthy AI use and preparation for the AI Act.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Financial supervisor's assessment of AI risks and AI Act readiness in the financial sector.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 22-page PDF read (pdftotext).

instruments.official_title: Uppdrag att vara nationella behöriga myndigheter enligt AI-förordningen
instruments.english_title: Assignment to act as national competent authorities under the AI Act
instruments.current_status: Government decision of 4 June 2026 (decision III:50); the assignment runs until 31 December 2026.
instruments.summary: Government decision (Fi2026/01365) assigning AI Act roles to national agencies: PTS is market surveillance authority for certain prohibited and high-risk uses (Annex III points 2-4, 5a and 5d, and radio equipment), single point of contact, is to set up an AI regulatory sandbox under Article 57 and supervises Article 50(1), (2) and (4) transparency obligations; IMY covers the remaining prohibited practices, Annex III points 1, 5b (in part) and 6-8, and Article 50(3); Finansinspektionen covers Annex III points 5b (within its supervised activities) and 5c; Läkemedelsverket covers AI in medical and in vitro diagnostic devices and is notifying authority for them; Swedac is the general notifying authority. It refers to SOU 2025:101, which proposed these designations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government decision designating Sweden's interim AI Act market surveillance and notifying authorities and single point of contact, and tasking PTS with setting up an AI regulatory sandbox.

instruments.english_title: The Police's and Swedish Customs' use of AI for post remote biometric identification (Ds 2025:32)
instruments.current_status: Published 19 December 2025 and sent for consultation (Ju2025/02805); 27 consultation responses are published on regeringen.se. No Lagrådsremiss or government bill is listed in the legislative chain.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Justice memorandum proposing a new law establishing an authorisation procedure, as required by Article 26(10) of the AI Act, under which the Police Authority, the Security Service and Swedish Customs may in certain cases be permitted to use AI systems for post remote biometric identification in criminal investigations, mainly for targeted searches for persons suspected or convicted of crimes. instruments.official_title: Ansvarsfull användning av AI i hälso- och sjukvården – Insikter och förslag från en förstudie med bröstcancerscreening som exempel
instruments.english_title: Responsible use of AI in health care: insights and proposals from a pre-study using breast cancer screening as an example
instruments.issuing_authority: National Board of Health and Welfare (Socialstyrelsen)
instruments.publisher_name: National Board of Health and Welfare
instruments.current_status: Published on socialstyrelsen.se in September 2026 as a pre-study report; it states that the proposals are not about creating new technology-specific regulation.
instruments.summary: Socialstyrelsen pre-study report (art. no. 2026-9-10396, with AI Sweden and Region Örebro län, funded by Vinnova) that uses breast cancer screening to set out seven guiding principles for responsible AI in health care: patient safety, work environment, equitable care, regulatory compliance, transparency, economy and long-term value creation, and knowledge and competence development. It proposes that Socialstyrelsen take a clearer normative role by clarifying how existing regulations on management systems and medical technology apply to AI and issuing support on responsible AI linked to the principles, national indicators for AI-supported breast cancer screening, uniform support for informing patients, and a joint guidance structure with Läkemedelsverket, IVO, E-hälsomyndigheten, IMY and SBU.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Health agency's principles for responsible AI in health care and proposals for its own normative role on AI.
instruments.evidence_reference: deep-sweep 2026-11-07: WebFetch of the PDF: title 'Ansvarsfull användning av AI i hälso- och sjukvården', 'Publicerad: www.socialstyrelsen.se, september 2026', article number 2026-9-10396; 'Sju principer för ansvarsfull AI' listed verbatim; next-step proposals for Socialstyrelsen.

instruments.english_title: AI regulatory sandbox: report on a pilot project (ES2026-01)
instruments.issuing_authority: eSamverkansprogrammet (eSam), together with the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY)
instruments.current_status: Final report dated February 2026 (an interim report ES2024-14 was published in 2024). eSam is a voluntary cooperation programme of Swedish government agencies; the report's assessments are hypothetical and not binding.
instruments.summary: Final report of a public-sector pilot run within eSam together with IMY, with Bolagsverket, Skatteverket, Arbetsförmedlingen, Ekonomistyrningsverket, Riksarkivet, Försäkringskassan and PTS taking part, that tested in four iterations what an AI Act regulatory sandbox requires, using hypothetical questions under the Regulation. It concludes that the AI Act is manageable legislation, that documentation for high-risk systems is administratively heavy, and that running sandboxes needs substantial access to skilled staff; technical support is not required by the AI Act but would make a sandbox attractive.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Cross-agency pilot of an AI Act regulatory sandbox for the Swedish public sector, run with the data protection authority.
instruments.evidence_reference: deep-sweep 2026-11-07: WebFetch of the PDF on esamverka.se: title 'AI-regulatorisk sandlåda – redovisning av pilotprojekt', 'Februari 2026', document number ES2026-01; IMY led the pilot with eSam; participants listed.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Sweden's laws (through the parliament's database), the Government, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for cybersecurity, standards or international agreements. Some official sites, including the official statute book and a government policy page, were unavailable, and the post and telecom, civil contingencies and competition authorities, the health, defence and education bodies and the standards institute are still to be checked in depth.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. svenskforfattningssamling.se 403 (laws read from the riksdagen.se SFS database); government.se policy page 403 (English PDFs reachable). PTS, MSB/NCSC and Konkurrensverket AI documents and SIS adoptions not reached; education, health and defence one discovery search only. 2018 approach kept as published (no official statement that the 2026 strategy replaces it). Convention 108: SÖ 1982:50, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: riksdagen.se open-data SFS/prop/bet search (AI-förordningen, artificiell intelligens, AI-system): found Act 2026:806 and Ordinance 2026:815 (real-time facial recognition), Ordinance 2026:1769 (Digitaliseringsmyndigheten), plus Administrative Procedure Act s.28 (automated decisions) and Data Protection Act 2018:218. No general AI Act implementing law yet (SOU 2025:101 at consultation stage; lead). svenskforfattningssamling.se blocked automated access (403); riksdagen.se SFS database used instead.; Government: regeringen.se: AI Strategy and action plan (Feb 2026), 2018 national approach, SOU 2025:12, SOU 2025:101, Dir. 2026:116 (lead), Ds 2025:32 (lead).; Ministries: Finance (digitalisation, strategy) and Justice (facial recognition law, public-access inquiry) covered; education/health/defence: one discovery search, no ministry-level AI document verified (Skolverket guidance held as lead).; Regulators: IMY (GenAI GDPR report), Digg (GenAI guidelines), Finansinspektionen (AI survey report). PTS/MSB/Konkurrensverket: no AI-specific document searched in depth.. Not reached: PTS, MSB/NCSC, Konkurrensverket AI-specific documents; Health (Socialstyrelsen, eHälsomyndigheten), defence and education ministry AI documents beyond one discovery search; Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS) AI standard adoptions. Could not verify: svenskforfattningssamling.se (official gazette) returned HTTP 403 to automated access; laws read from the riksdagen.se SFS database instead.; government.se policy HTML page returned 403 (the English PDFs were reachable).. cyber-security, standards, international: no material found.
Sweep 2026-11-13: IMY press release of 5 November 2026 announces a supervisory review of Arbetsförmedlingen's AI system (single-organisation supervision, no decision yet; not recorded). pts.se news URL 404; not checked further within the cap.
